newsitem.title: UGANDA: World coffee body to help fight against wilt pest.
newsitem.headline: World coffee body to help fight against wilt pest.

text.p: The International Coffee Organization is ready to fund a scientific project aimed at fighting a coffee wilt disease devastating the crop in east and central Africa, a senior ICO official said on Tuesday.

Julia Elena Serpa told Reuters on the sidelines of a conference called to discuss methods of containing the tracheomycosis diease, that it was spreading fast and threatening the livelihood of many people.
The disease is active in Uganda, where it has hit 12 coffee-growing districts, and in the Democratic Republic of the Congo where it was first located in the 1950s.
The ICO, which groups world coffee producers and consumers, "will support any project which comes up as we want to see the eradication of the problem in the region," Serpa said.
She added: "The problem is a very serious one indeed. Control measures need to be formulated fast to check it as coffee is the mainstay of most of our economies."

Up to 70 representatives from African coffee producing nations and researchers from the International Mycological Institute (IMI) are meeting in the Ugandan capital to draw up a programme of action against the disease.

Tracheomycosis destroys a coffee tree's vascular system. It leaves a black sear on the tree stem after which the tree dies. Lack of scientific research and a well defined programme has meant that the wilt has spread freely in the region.

At present, coffee farmers only uproot affected trees once the disease has been located in an area. Uganda's government policy is also to uproot and burn down all affected trees and then keep affected areas free from the crop for two years. It then arranges free seedlings for farmers to replant.
Uganda has also launched a quarantine system restricting movement of robusta coffee tusks across districts. --Nairobi newsroom ++254 2 330-261
